name: thread-item
description:
One entry in a scrolling list of conversations, jobs or intents — the app's intent list, and the shape any inbox is. A title that truncates, a preview line under it, and a timestamp pinned to the trailing edge.

What makes it a unit rather than a row: the SELECTED state inverts the whole item, and everything inside it has to follow. The app spelled that as a ternary on every child — `{sel ? 'text-current' : ''}`, `{sel ? 'opacity-75' : 'text-foreground/50'}`, `{sel ? 'opacity-60' : 'text-foreground/35'}` — three conditionals to say one thing, and three places for the selected treatment to drift from itself.

title.$description: Truncates. A list of these is scanned rather than read, and a two-line title in one row and a one-line title in the next destroys the rhythm the scan depends on.

selected.$description: The whole item inverts, and `color: inherit` on the children is what carries it — the app wrote a ternary on each child instead, which is three places for one decision to drift.

reducedMotion.$description: The background still changes; it just changes at once.

a11y.note: `aria-current="true"` on the selected item, not colour alone — an inverted row is invisible to a screen reader. The timestamp is a `<time datetime>` where it is a real date, so 'yesterday' is announced as the date it means. Truncated titles keep their full text in the accessible name; a title that ends in an ellipsis for the eye must not end in one for the reader.
